title: Exam Week, One Day at a Time
pin_title: ADHD Exam Week Plan: How to Study Without Panic and Burnout
description: Exam week can trigger all-or-nothing studying. Break it into days: pick the three most important topics, give each a short block, add breaks with food and a walk, and finish with a small win. Sleep matters more than one extra hour of cramming. Review what went well each night and adjust gently. #ADHD #ExamPrep #ADHDStudent #StudyTips

title: Touch It Once
pin_title: The One-Touch Rule for ADHD: Stop Moving Clutter From Pile to Pile
description: Clutter grows when items get picked up and put down again. Try the one-touch rule: when you pick something up, put it where it belongs right away. If you cannot decide, use a basket labeled decide later and empty it weekly. Fewer touches means fewer piles. Start with just one room or one surface. #ADHD #Decluttering #ADHDLife

title: Guess, Then Add Half
pin_title: Time Blindness Hack: Multiply Your Time Guess by 1.5 for ADHD Planning
description: ADHD brains tend to underestimate how long things take. Try the 1.5 rule: write down your guess, add half again, and schedule that. A task you guess at 20 minutes gets 30. Then note the real time to learn your pattern. Extra buffer means less rushing, and less rushing means less stress. #ADHD #TimeBlindness #Planning

title: A Kind Way to Say No
pin_title: How to Say No When You Have ADHD: Kind Scripts That Protect Your Energy
description: Saying yes feels easy in the moment and costs you later. Keep a few scripts ready: let me check my calendar and get back to you, thank you for thinking of me but I cannot take that on, I can help with this smaller part. A short pause protects your energy and your reputation. #ADHD #Boundaries #ADHDTips

title: Group Projects Made Easier
pin_title: ADHD Group Project Tips: Simple Roles and Check-Ins for Students
description: Group projects need coordination, which is hard when planning is your challenge. Offer to take a clear role, share a simple checklist with dates and agree on one short check-in per week. Write down who does what in the chat so nothing is lost. Clear small steps keep the group moving. #ADHD #ADHDStudent #StudyTips

title: Before the Appointment Checklist
pin_title: ADHD Appointment Checklist: Get Ready on Time Without the Stress
description: Appointments can create anxious waiting mode. Work backward: set the leaving time, add a thirty-minute buffer, gather what you need the night before and set two alarms. Use the gap before for one tiny task only. Having a clear plan frees your mind from watching the clock. #ADHD #ADHDChecklist #TimeManagement

title: Track Habits Without Streaks
pin_title: ADHD Habit Tracker Tips: Track Progress Without the Shame of Broken Streaks
description: A streak counter can turn one missed day into a reason to quit. Track habits by how many days you did them this week instead, and count a partial effort as a win. Seeing four out of seven shows real progress and keeps you coming back. Let the tracker support you, not scold you. #ADHD #HabitTracker #ADHDLife #SmallWins

title: Ask the Clarifying Question
pin_title: ADHD at Work: Clarifying Questions That Save Hours of Guesswork
description: Vague instructions create anxiety and rework. Ask one clarifying question right away: what does done look like, who needs this, and by when. Repeat back what you heard in one sentence and write it down. A thirty-second question can save a day of worry and builds trust. #ADHD #ADHDatWork #Communication

title: Quiz Yourself in Short Bursts
pin_title: ADHD Study Method: Active Recall in Five-Minute Bursts for Better Memory
description: Rereading notes feels productive but fades fast. Try active recall: close the book and write down everything you remember, then check what you missed. Do it in five-minute bursts with a timer. Short, active sessions hold attention better and make studying feel like a game. #ADHD #StudyTips #ADHDStudent #ActiveRecall

title: Reaching Out After a Long Gap
pin_title: ADHD Friendships: How to Reconnect After Weeks of Silence Without Guilt
description: Many ADHD adults go quiet with friends and then feel too guilty to reach out. Send a short, warm message: I have been thinking of you, no pressure to reply. Skip the long apology. Most people are happy to hear from you, and a small check-in reopens the door. Your friends would love to hear from you, truly. #ADHD #Friendship #ADHDLife

title: Receive Feedback Gently
pin_title: ADHD and Feedback at Work: How to Listen Without Spiraling
description: Critical feedback can feel enormous with ADHD. Try three steps: breathe, write down the exact words and wait before reacting. Ask which part matters most and what a good next step looks like. Separate the task from your worth. Feedback is information, not a verdict. #ADHD #ADHDatWork #SelfCompassion

title: Pick Outfit Defaults
pin_title: ADHD Wardrobe Tip: Outfit Defaults That Save Morning Energy
description: Choosing clothes costs energy and time. Set up a few go-to outfits that feel comfortable and match each other, and keep them together on one shelf. Use a weekly rotation or lay out tomorrow's outfit tonight. Less deciding means more energy for the day ahead. Your future morning self will thank you. #ADHD #DecisionFatigue #MorningRoutine

title: The Brain Fog List
pin_title: ADHD Brain Fog Tasks: A List of Low-Demand Things for Foggy Days
description: Some days thinking feels like wading through mud. Keep a list of low-demand tasks ready: water the plants, wipe a counter, sort mail, rename a few files. Doing something small gives a sense of progress without needing deep focus. Fog passes and the list waits. Rest if you need it, and try again later. #ADHD #BrainFog #LowEnergy
